lemonde.title: Marine Le Pen candidate à la présidentielle de 2027 : le mythe du « phénix » de l’extrême droite

lemonde.title: Aide à mourir : le Sénat renonce définitivement à modifier le texte de l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Pour la troisième fois, le Palais du Luxembourg a rejeté, mardi, la proposition de loi, la droite sénatoriale, majoritaire avec ses alliés centristes, jugeant les critères retenus par les députés beaucoup trop larges. Ces derniers auront le dernier mot, le 15 juillet, en vue d’une adoption définitive.

lemonde.title: « Je me sens salie, humiliée » : au procès de l’administrateur de CFake, site de deepfakes à caractère sexuel
lemonde.description: Un informaticien niçois a été reconnu coupable, mardi 7 juillet, d’avoir administré cette plateforme de montages et hypertrucages pornographiques mettant en scène des personnalités. Il a notamment été condamné à deux ans de prison, dont un avec sursis, ainsi qu’à 83 000 euros pour les parties civiles.

lemonde.title: La Suisse élimine la Colombie en huitièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde grâce à la prestation de son gardien, Gregor Kobel
lemonde.description: Il a fallu attendre les tirs au but, mardi, pour départager les deux équipes (0-0, 4-3 t.a.b). Seule la sélection argentine représentera le football sud-américain en quarts de finale du Mondial, une première depuis 2002.

lemonde.title: « Je n’ai pas vécu le Covid, ç’a été ma première crise sanitaire » : la canicule, un baptême du feu pour les externes en médecine

lemonde.title: La Turquie, un allié encombrant devenu partenaire indispensable au sein de l’OTAN
lemonde.description: Après s’être rapproché de la Russie dans les années 2010, le pays a resserré ses liens avec Washington et plusieurs capitales européennes. Le sommet de l’OTAN à Ankara, mardi et mercredi, acte la considération dont jouit le président Recep Tayipp Erdogan aux yeux des Occidentaux, malgré l’évolution de plus en plus autoritaire de son régime.

lemonde.description: Les députés de gauche, dénonçant un potentiel « permis de tuer », ont tenté d’empêcher le vote par un barrage d’amendements, contourné par le gouvernement à l’aide d’un article constitutionnel.

lemonde.title: Mortalité périnatale : malgré des chiffres toujours inquiétants, les causes restent encore à explorer
lemonde.description: En 2024, le nombre d’enfants nés sans vie ou décédés au cours des sept premiers jours, a atteint 11,2 pour 1 000 naissances, contre 10,8 l’année précédente, selon une note de la direction statistique des ministères sociaux.

lemonde.title: Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans : la France doit retravailler son texte pour se conformer au droit européen
lemonde.description: La Commission européenne a rendu mardi 7 juillet son avis sur la proposition de loi interdisant les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans. Si elle autorise la France à établir un âge minimal d’accès à ces plateformes, elle demande à voir modifiés certains points. Le gouvernement espère faire appliquer le texte dès septembre.

lemonde.description: Héritières des « hatago » historiques, ces auberges vantent une culture d’accueil et de service uniques. Elles s’adaptent aux demandes des touristes occidentaux, avec le risque de s’éloigner de leur promesse initiale.

france24fr.description: Le géant sud-coréen Samsung a connu une chute en Bourse de près de 6 % alors même que ses profits augmentent de 1 800 %. observador.description: Há quem aproveite o calor para suar mais e por acreditar que queima mais calorias. Mas quando o termómetro anda na casa dos 30 graus, o exercício pode transformar-se num verdadeiro teste ao organismo.

observador.title: Retratos de quem faz o Museu do Caramulo acontecer
observador.description: O simples pedido de José Maçãs de Carvalho: usar o Museu do Caramulo como inspiração para criações originais. Do desafio nasceram retratos dos trabalhadores do espaço, de costas, por Daniela Krtsch.

observador.title: A crise da água às portas de Lisboa
observador.description: Há dias que milhares de pessoas em Almada vivem com cortes de água. A jornalista Marina Ferreira explica o que está na origem desta crise e quem assume responsabilidades.

observador.title: 4h. EUA lançam novos ataques ao Irão
observador.description: Washington diz que a operação serve para travar os ataques iranianos contra o comércio internacional. Ainda, A cimeira da NATO na Turquia termina esta quarta-feira.

observador.title: 3h. Incêndio no Sabugal mobiliza perto de 350 bombeiros
observador.description: O presidente da autarquia espera que o incêndio fique dominado ainda esta noite. Ainda, Teerão não confirma nem desmente as acusações de ataques contra navios comerciais.

observador.title: 2h. Teerão reafirma o controlo sobre o Estreito de Ormuz
observador.description: E não confirma nem desmente as acusações de ataques contra navios comerciais. Ainda, a Suíça venceu a Colômbia e está nos quartos de final do Campeonato do Mundo.

observador.title: 1h. Trump avisa que ataques no Irão são para continuar
observador.description: Washington diz que a operação visa impor "custos pesados" a Teerão. Ainda, dois feridos na sequência de um ataque com mísseis russos à capital ucraniana.

observador.title: Após ataques em Ormuz, EUA "castigam" e voltam atacar o Irão
observador.description: EUA lançaram uma "série de ataques poderosos" contra o Irão esta noite para "impor custos pesados" ao Irão por Teerão ter atacado embarcações no Estreito de Ormuz. Há registo de feridos.

observador.title: O suicídio económico da Europa chama-se transição climática
observador.description: Decadência industrial, dependência da China e empobrecimento das classes médias. Eis os resultados das políticas climáticas europeias.

observador.title: Ninguém queria enfrentar Messi e a sacrificada foi a Suiça
observador.description: Suiça eliminou Colômbia nos penáltis e segue para os quartos de final. Alpes Suiços trouxeram a frieza necessária para Kobel defender e Vargas sentenciar a eliminatória na marca dos 11 metros.

observador.title: A crise da imigração: do negacionismo à remigração
observador.description: O tema dos fluxos migratórios e suas consequências está para ficar e não deve ser ignorado, em especial por quem coloca a dignidade da pessoa humana no centro das suas preocupações.

observador.title: A coligação
observador.description: É a coligação entre poder autárquico, associações de bombeiros, protecção civil e jornalismo que tem mantido um conjunto de mitos inúteis sobre a gestão de fogos

observador.title: Teoria da substituição: de Martínez a Sánchez
observador.description: De Espanha, nem bom vento, nem boas substituições. O Martínez teimou em não substituir portugueses cansados e Pedro Sánchez não descansa enquanto não substituir todos os espanhóis que não votam PSOE.

observador.title: Que fazer com um milhão de pessoas?
observador.description: A imigração é um daqueles casos em que “por um lado isto, por outro lado aquilo…”.  A economia portuguesa revelou-se muito dinâmica, mas a fazer mais do mesmo ou ainda pior.

observador.title: Ao entrar no Supremo
observador.description: A mais alta instância comum não se legitima pela distância, mas pela clareza das razões que oferece, pelo diálogo que aceita e por um humanismo que a técnica não dispensa.

observador.title: A velha questão do populismo
observador.description: Mesmo que não ganhem as eleições, porque a luta é desigual, os partidos exteriores ao sistema oligárquico-partidário, pela sua própria existência, já desempenham um papel fundamental na democracia.

spiegel.title: Bäckereien: Insolvenzen nehmen deutlich zu
spiegel.description: Innerhalb von zehn Jahren ist die Zahl der Bäckereiunternehmen stark gesunken. Nun zieht auch das Insolvenzgeschehen an. Branchenexperten sehen andere Betriebe als Gewinner.

spiegel.title: Attestpflicht ab erstem Krankheitstag? Sie müssen jetzt ganz stark sein (und gesund) - Essay von Margarete Stokowski
spiegel.description: Attestpflicht ab dem ersten Krankheitstag? Dahinter steckt eine menschenverachtende Botschaft.

spiegel.title: Krankschreibungen: Alexander Schweitzer kritisiert Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz
spiegel.description: »Sätze wie vom Kasernenhof«: In der Debatte über die Reform der Bundesregierung wünscht sich Ex-Ministerpräsident Schweitzer einen anderen Ton vom Kanzler. Der SPD-Politiker plädiert für pragmatische Lösungen.

spiegel.title: Ungarn - Viktor Orbán: Staatliches Radio und Fernsehen stellen Sendebetrieb ein
spiegel.description: »Die öffentlich-rechtlichen Medien dürfen nicht lügen. Es tut uns leid, dass wir es so lange getan haben«: In Ungarn wickelt die neue Regierung die alte ab und reformiert die Staatspresse.

spiegel.title: Mehr als 300 Kinder im Sudan seit Jahresbeginn getötet
spiegel.description: Sie sind zwischen zwei Monaten und 17 Jahren alt: Die Konfliktparteien im Sudan töten auch viele Kinder. Die Waffe der Wahl? Immer häufiger Drohnen.

spiegel.title: Frankreich will Syrien Millionen aus Assad-Vermögen zurückgeben
spiegel.description: Emmanuel Macron hat Syrien als erster westlicher Staatschef besucht – samt großer Wirtschaftsdelegation. Der Chef des Energiekonzerns TotalEnergies bezeichnet das Ex-Bürgerkriegsland bereits als mögliche Alternative zur Straße von Hormus.

spiegel.title: Bürgerrechts-Aktivistin Mary Church Terrell: »Gejagt und abgeschlachtet wie wilde Tiere«
spiegel.description: Die Sklaventochter Mary Church Terrell kämpfte gegen Lynchterror, Diskriminierung und Vorurteile in den USA, setzte sich für die Rechte der Afroamerikaner ein. Die Trump-Ära könnte die Erfolge der Pionierin zurückdrehen.

spiegel.title: Zweibrücken: Urteil im Prozess um zu Tode geprügelten Zugbegleiter steht bevor
spiegel.description: Im Prozess gegen einen 26-Jährigen, der im Februar einen Zugbegleiter in den Tod geprügelt hat, steht das Urteil bevor. Für die Angehörigen des Opfers sind die Verhandlungstermine schwer zu ertragen.

spiegel.title: »Little People, Big Dreams«: Die Kinderbuchreihe erklärt selbst Dreijährige zu potenziellen Genies. Muss das sein?
Studie: KI-Modell Claude zitiert russisches Desinformations-Netz als Nachrichtenquelle
spiegel.description: Immer mehr Menschen nutzen KI als Nachrichtenquelle und hoffen auf neutrale und objektive Antworten. Nun warnt eine neue Studie vor »schwer wahrnehmbaren Verzerrungen« durch die Modelle von Anthropic, OpenAI und Co.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: Neues Militär-Hauptquartier so groß wie Lissabon
spiegel.description: Das Pentagon ist klein dagegen: Ägyptens Machthaber Abdel Fattah el-Sisi hat seinen Militärs eine Megaimmobilie geschenkt, auf die Donald Trump neidisch sein dürfte.

spiegel.title: News: Nato-Gipfel in Ankara, Donald Trump, Gesundheits-Sparpaket, TV-Fußball-Experten
spiegel.description: In Ankara wird es ernst beim Nato-Gipfel. Das Gesundheitssparpaket sorgt für mehr Druck auf Langzeitkranke. Und bei der WM ist heute spielfrei: Zeit, die besten TV-Fußballexperten zu küren. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochmorgen.

spiegel.title: Rente: So viel zusätzliche Schwedenrente ist für Sie möglich
spiegel.description: Die geplante Kapitalrente nach schwedischem Vorbild soll die gesetzliche Rente ergänzen. Hier können Sie ausprobieren, mit wie viel Geld Sie im Alter rechnen können.

spiegel.title: Erling Haaland: DJ Kygo legt zehn Jahre alten Rap-Song des Norwegen-Fußballers neu auf
spiegel.description: Erling Haaland ist spätestens seit der WM als Fußballhüne weltbekannt. Als noch schmächtiger 15-Jähriger versuchte sich der Norweger einst an einem Rap-Song – der nun mit seiner Zustimmung als Remix veröffentlicht wurde. Ohrwurmalarm!

spiegel.title: Nato-Generalsekretär Rutte bezeichnet US-Angriffe auf Iran als »absolut notwendig«
spiegel.description: Washington macht Teheran für die jüngsten Angriffe auf Tanker in der Straße von Hormus verantwortlich. Jetzt meldet das US-Militär massive Attacken auf iranische Ziele. Das Regime reagiert mit Gegenschlägen auf Bahrain und Kuwait.

spiegel.title: New York: Hochhaus mitten in Manhattan wegen Einsturzgefahr geräumt
spiegel.description: Eingeknickte Stützpfeiler, abgesackte Decken: Mitten in Manhattan muss ein 37-stöckiges Gebäude geräumt werden. Es wird gerade umgebaut. Entwarnung gibt es bislang nicht.

spiegel.title: Houston: ICE-Beamter erschießt mexikanischen Einwanderer
spiegel.description: Bei einer Razzia gegen Einwanderer ist in Houston ein Mexikaner getötet worden. Der Mann soll angeblich versucht haben, einen Beamten mit seinem Auto zu erfassen. Bürgerrechtler fordern eine unabhängige Untersuchung.

spiegel.title: Mitch McConnell: Top-Republikaner seit Wochen im Krankenhaus - Gerüchte über Gesundheit
spiegel.description: Vor fast vier Wochen wurde Republikaner-Urgestein Mitch McConnell ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert. Seitdem wurde der 84-Jährige öffentlich nicht gesehen, sein Büro hält sich äußerst bedeckt. Die Opposition heizt Gerüchte an.

elpais.title: La última victoria ideológica de Ayuso: lo que dice (y lo que no) la ley del concebido no nacido
elpais.description: La norma permite que el embrión compute como hijo a efectos de ayudas y el título de familia numerosa, una medida que expertos y oposición consideran un precedente ideológico

nyt.title: Oil Prices Jump After Renewed Strikes in Gulf Put Shipping Recovery at Risk
nyt.description: Attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz sparked a new cycle of retaliation that could throttle the flow of energy from the region.

nyt.title: As Israel Loses Support in the U.S., Rahm Emanuel Criticizes Netanyahu
nyt.description: The former Chicago mayor, a Democrat exploring a 2028 presidential run, is in Tel Aviv calling for an end to unconditional U.S. support of Israel.

nyt.title: Trump’s arrival in Turkey for NATO summit adds drama and spectacle
nyt.description: The second President Trump landed in Turkey, the center of gravity shifted right to where he likes it best: himself.

nyt.title: NATO Allies Show Trump They Are Trying to Pay Up for Defense
nyt.description: Some countries are making significant progress on raising their military spending. A few are stretching the definition of military spending to try to meet their targets.

nyt.title: What to Know About the ‘Frozen Zone’ in Midtown Manhattan
nyt.description: A building at risk of partial collapse prompted the city to restrict pedestrian and vehicle traffic in the area. Some buses were diverted or delayed, but subway lines remained uninterrupted.

nyt.title: Haley Stevens Goes on Attack Against Abdul El-Sayed at Michigan Senate Debate
nyt.description: At their first one-on-one debate in a top Senate race, Representative Haley Stevens accused her progressive rival, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, of being too focused on publicity as he called her a tool of corporate interests.

nyt.title: New Rules Require Election Changes for States to Get Terrorism Grants
nyt.description: Federal officials said they would withhold some money unless states pursue paper ballot systems, verify citizenship and conduct costly audits.

nyt.title: Top Maine Democrat Says Platner Will Have ‘No Role’ in Picking Next Nominee
nyt.description: A top state party official said that Graham Platner’s team had “repeatedly” tried to “put their thumb on the scale,” but he would not influence how the party chose a new Senate candidate.

nyt.title: These Maine Democrats Might Replace Graham Platner in the Senate Race
nyt.description: Mr. Platner has not yet withdrawn from the race after a rape allegation, but Democrats in the state and nationally are already exploring potential alternatives.

nyt.title: Marine Le Pen’s Court Battle Is Latest Clash Between Populists and Watchdogs
nyt.description: The far-right leader’s battle with the French judiciary evokes standoffs across the populist world, including ones with President Trump and Nigel Farage.

nyt.title: Le Pen Says She Will Run for Presidency After Court Lifts Ban
nyt.description: An appeals court confirmed Marine Le Pen’s embezzlement conviction, but shortened a ban on her eligibility for elected office. That means the French far-right leader can run for president in 2027.

nyt.title: The World Cup Stood as a Break From U.S. Politics. Then Trump Got Involved.
nyt.description: The president’s call to the head of FIFA underscores that he has yet to find an area of American, or even global, life where he is unwilling to assert himself.

nyt.title: ICE Officer Kills a Mexican Man in Houston
nyt.description: The agency said the man was an “illegal alien” who had tried to run over the agent, though no evidence was immediately offered.

nyt.title: Judge Orders D.H.S. to Restore 4 States’ Access to Citizenship Data
nyt.description: The ruling, based on an agreement the Trump administration signed with Florida last year, contradicted an earlier order by a judge in Washington that required the access be suspended.

nyt.title: Yale Law School Fights to Stop Trump Deal
nyt.description: The university has been in talks to resolve investigations into its admissions practices. The law school’s dean and some faculty have argued a deal could compromise its independence.

nyt.title: Andrea Shaw, Plaintiff in Anti-Vaccine Suit, Is Charged With Murder of Her Twins
nyt.description: A lawsuit filed by Children’s Health Defense, an organization founded by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., claims that vaccines caused the twins’ deaths. But a grand jury in Idaho has indicted her on charges of suffocating them.

nyt.title: Suspect Interacted With Charlie Kirk’s Group Before Killing, Prosecutors Say
nyt.description: In a hearing, prosecutors used videos to trace the steps of the man they accuse of assassinating Mr. Kirk, while defense lawyers tried to poke holes in DNA evidence.

nyt.title: Germans Don’t Love Budweiser. It Won’t Take No for an Answer.
nyt.description: Not for the first time, Budweiser is trying to make it in Germany. But this is a tough time to sell German drinkers on the image and taste of American beer.

npr.title: What happened in the opening day of the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey
npr.description: NATO arrived in Ankara with a message of unity, but President Trump's renewed attacks on European allies have once again laid bare the tensions challenging the alliance's future.

npr.title: What's at stake at the NATO summit in Turkey
npr.description: NATO leaders hope President Trump's criticism of the alliance is aimed at getting Europe to spend more on defense. But some analysts fear Trump may have an ulterior motive.

npr.title: IOC moves to allow more Russian athletes back into the Olympic games
npr.description: The IOC is moving to clear the way for Russian athletes to compete in Olympic events. The decision to ease sanctions comes as Moscow continues missile and drone strikes killing civilians in Ukraine.

npr.title: International Olympic Committee lifts Russia suspension ahead of 2028 LA Games
npr.description: The International Olympic Committee advised sports bodies to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

npr.title: Woman accuses Graham Platner of sexual assault. And, NATO summit begins
npr.description: Graham Platner is facing calls to end his bid for U.S. Senate in Maine after a woman accused him of sexual assault. And, Trump made his dissatisfaction with NATO clear ahead of its summit this week.

npr.title: Ukraine to press NATO for anti-ballistic air defense after latest Russian attacks
npr.description: Ukraine pushes allies in NATO for anti-ballistic air defense after the latest major Russian attacks kill more than 20 in Kyiv and surrounding area.

npr.title: Trump's NATO pressure campaign continues as summit begins
npr.description: President Trump's arrival in Ankara kicks off another potentially tense meeting for NATO.

npr.title: Explosions rock Damascus, wounding 18, as French President Macron visits Syria
npr.description: The French president's office said that Macron was safe and that his meeting with Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa would continue as scheduled.

npr.title: NATO summit set to begin in Turkey
npr.description: Ahead of the  NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, the illusion of appeasing Trump has vanished—and Europe is being forced to take primary responsibility for its own defense.

npr.title: Former U.S. ambassador on Turkey hosting the NATO summit
npr.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to Turkey David Satterfield about the significance of Turkey hosting the NATO summit.

lanacion.description: La víctima recibió un piedrazo en la cabeza y fue trasladada a un hospital de la zona, donde llegó sin signos vitales

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

proj-syn.title: In Praise of the World Cup’s Little Guys
proj-syn.description: In a world of great-power rivalry and hyper-scaling tech behemoths, you would be forgiven for thinking that the bulky bully always has the edge. But as this year's World Cup has shown repeatedly, you would be wrong.

proj-syn.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
proj-syn.description: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.

proj-syn.title: Just Say No to Remote Work
proj-syn.description: Even during the immediate post-pandemic period, when evidence on the labor-market effects of remote work was scant, there was a strong case to be made for going into the office, especially for younger workers. And now, multiple new studies have vindicated this intuition.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. If Germany, in particular, insists on going it alone, Europe could remain fully dependent on the US for key assets.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.
